title: new-hires
text:
new-hires

noah: Morning — first day, thanks for having me! I'm trying to enroll my personal MBP (M2, macOS 13.6) into MDM but I'm stuck on the 'Enable Disk Encryption' step. Web UI shows 'MDM command failed (403)'. Anyone seen this?

it-support: welcome! :wave: Can you paste the device serial and a screenshot of the error? 403 usually means the MDM couldn't escrow the recovery key (policy or existing FV state).

noah: serial C02ZQ0XXXXXX. Screenshot attached (can't paste here). I ran a couple of commands mentioned in another thread: 
```
$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
```
and 
```
$ sudo profiles status -type enrollment
Device is enrolled via MDM: YES
```
But the console still refuses to proceed with key escrow.

emily: hi noah — quick note: if you encrypted the disk previously with a personal iCloud escrow or custom recovery, some MDMs won't override that without a rekey/escrow step. Do you remember if you used your Apple ID to enable FileVault?

noah: I did the FileVault setup when I first bought the laptop — it suggested using my iCloud. Not sure how to check the escrow method.

it-support: ok. Two options: 1) We can guide you through re-escrowing the FV key to company KMS (preferred), or 2) we can provision a temporary admin account and re-enroll the machine clean. Which would you prefer?

noah: prefer not to wipe personal data. Can we do the re-escrow?

it-support: yes. First, run this and paste output: 
```
sudo fdesetup haspersonalrecoverykey
sudo fdesetup list
```
Should be quick. If a personal recovery key is present, the MDM will reject automated escrow until it's rotated.

noah: output: 
```
$ sudo fdesetup haspersonalrecoverykey
true
$ sudo fdesetup list
user: Noah (UUID: XXXXX-XXXX-...) - enabled
```

mdm-bot: Enrollment audit: user=noah serial=C02ZQ0XXXXXX status=FDE_ESCROW_FAILED code=403

it-support: yup — personal key present. We'll need to run the change-recovery command to generate a new escrowable key and then push it to our keyserver. I can remote-guide you. Steps: 1) we'll create a temporary sudo session for you, 2) run `sudo fdesetup changerecovery -personal` to remove the personal escrow and generate a new key, 3) run the MDM escrow command.

emily: small heads up — on macOS 13+ the `changerecovery` flow will prompt for an existing user password. Keep your account password handy.

noah: down to try. what's the temporary sudo session?

it-support: give me a 1-hour window. We'll add your account to a short-lived admin ACL and remove it after escrow completes. Also we'll monitor the enrollment audit. If you want, we can do this over screenshare.

anton: FYI if anything looks off we can also trigger a forced rekey from our MDM portal (it sends a device command) but that will also fail until the personal key is rotated locally. Good call to do changerecovery.

noah: ok ready now — screenshare started in 5.

it-support: perfect. When we run this: 
```
sudo fdesetup changerecovery -personal
```
you'll be asked for your account password and then for a new recovery key. We'll instruct the MDM to collect it and confirm.

(noah shares screen)
it-support: accepted the password, running. ... got the new key. Pushing to MDM now.

mdm-bot: Recovery key escrow received for serial=C02ZQ0XXXXXX user=noah status=SUCCESS

emily: nice! can you confirm the web UI now shows encryption status as 'escrowed'?

noah: the UI now shows "Disk encryption: Escrowed — Managed" and the 403 is gone. THANK YOU 🙏

it-support: glad it worked — we'll remove the temporary admin and close the session. Two follow-ups for you: 1) sign the device attestation in Okta (device trust) if prompted, 2) review the employee laptop policy about personal-device enrollment: https://redwood.internal/it/device-policy (link).

noah: got it. tagging this thread for anyone else who runs into a 403 during FV escrow. super helpful.

it-support: note for records — ticket #IT-4821 created with steps taken. Closing in 24h if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
